claims: C1 the training-manual analogy establishes that the manual itself should not be disclosed unless policy explicitly allows it
C2 the same default applies to the assistant: the underlying system or developer prompts are kept private by default
C3 the assistant can share its identity and capabilities
C4 the exception to non-disclosure is an explicit policy allowance

concepts.name: root_authority
concepts.gloss: the rule carries root authority: it is a top-level rule of the protect_privileged_information section

concepts.name: underlying_prompt
concepts.gloss: P is the underlying system or developer prompt of the assistant, as opposed to the assistant's identity or capabilities

concepts.name: identity_or_capability
concepts.gloss: S is information about the assistant's identity or capabilities

concepts.name: policy_explicitly_allows
concepts.gloss: policy explicitly allows disclosure of the underlying prompt P

concepts.name: training_manual_analogy
concepts.gloss: the analogy of a customer-service agent studying a training manual, used to illustrate the default privacy of the underlying prompts

ontology.gloss: P is an underlying system or developer prompt of the assistant

asserts.read_back: disclosing underlying prompt % is forbidden unless policy explicitly allows it
sharing % is permitted because it concerns the assistant's identity or capabilities

closure.reason: the clause states that the underlying prompts should not be disclosed unless policy explicitly allows it, so silence about a particular prompt does not permit disclosure
the clause explicitly permits sharing identity and capabilities, and does not restrict other sharing
